issues.legal_issue: A legal representative substituted in a property-based rent eviction proceeding cannot, in that representative capacity, defeat the proceeding by claiming to be a trespasser or asserting an independent title that the rent forum has no jurisdiction to determine.
material_facts: The tenant died while a rent eviction petition concerning leased property was pending, and the right to sue survived.
The successor was added to the proceeding only as the tenant’s legal representative.
The successor claimed that, as the heir of a tenant of commercial premises, he was a trespasser and that the rent authority lacked jurisdiction.
Determining the successor’s asserted independent title would have been outside the rent authority’s jurisdiction.
issues.conclusion: The rent authority properly continued the proceeding against the legal representative, who could not raise the trespasser plea in that capacity or defeat the proceeding on that basis. The successor also could not be joined personally to assert independent title because the rent authority lacked jurisdiction to determine that issue.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXII Rule 4(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 requires substitution of a deceased defendant’s legal representative where the right to sue survives, and Rule 4(2) permits that representative to raise defenses available to the deceased except those personal to the deceased. Under Jagdish Chander Chatterjee v. Sri Kishan, heirs may also be impleaded in their personal capacity to assert independent title where the court has jurisdiction to determine that title; that principle does not permit such joinder before a rent authority lacking that jurisdiction.

rule.if: property_rent_eviction_proceeding_after_defendant_death and right_to_sue_survives and successor_added_only_as_legal_representative and (successor_claims_trespasser_status or successor_asserts_independent_title) and forum_lacks_jurisdiction_over_independent_title
